stem: The solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{2x}{x^2+1}y=2x$, satisfying $y(0)=1$, has $y(1)$ equal to

verdicts.working: Integrating factor is $x^2+1$, so $((x^2+1)y)'=2x(x^2+1)$. Using $y(0)=1$ gives $y(1)=\frac{5}{4}$.

working:
$\text{IF}=e^{\int \frac{2x}{x^2+1}\,dx}=x^2+1$.
$$\big((x^2+1)y\big)'=2x(x^2+1)$$
$$(x^2+1)y=\dfrac{(x^2+1)^2}{2}+C$$
$y(0)=1\implies C=\dfrac{1}{2}$.
$$y(1)=1+\dfrac{1}{4}=\dfrac{5}{4}$$ Independent check: Integrating factor is $x^2+1$, so $((x^2+1)y)'=2x(x^2+1)$. Using $y(0)=1$ gives $y(1)=\frac{5}{4}$.
